message.content: In domestic cats and many other felids, the **presence of a mane** (the long, dark fur that grows around the head and neck of male lions) is governed by a **dominant allele**. In lions, the allele that codes for a mane is dominant over the allele that codes for a lack of mane. Thus, if a lion inherits one copy of the mane allele from either parent, it will develop a mane. This dominant trait is also responsible for the typical **black coloration** of the mane, as the black allele masks any lighter or white alleles that might be present.
